```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(gt)
library(gtExtras)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

# Brand colors from _brand.yml
c_navy    <- "#303e4e"
c_teal    <- "#0f9a7d"
c_blue    <- "#3a6ea5"
c_orange  <- "#d1622a"
c_violet  <- "#6b4fb2"
c_ochre   <- "#a8820a"
c_red     <- "#c1393f"
c_green   <- "#7d9c33"
c_seq_1   <- "#eef1f4"

# Check if pipeline targets are accessible, else load robust demonstration data
has_targets <- tryCatch({
  tar_read(composite_rankings)
  TRUE
}, error = function(e) FALSE)

if (has_targets) {
  composite   <- tar_read(composite_rankings)
  benchmark   <- tar_read(benchmark_comparison)
  season_info <- tar_read(current_season_info)
  
  if (!"record" %in% names(composite)) {
    if (!is.null(benchmark$comparison_table) && all(c("wins", "losses") %in% names(benchmark$comparison_table))) {
      rec_lookup <- benchmark$comparison_table |> dplyr::select(team, wins, losses) |> dplyr::distinct()
      composite <- composite |> dplyr::left_join(rec_lookup, by = "team") |>
        dplyr::mutate(record = ifelse(!is.na(wins), paste0(wins, "-", losses), "-"))
    } else {
      composite$record <- "-"
    }
  }

  if (!is.null(benchmark$comparison_table) && nrow(benchmark$comparison_table) > 0) {
    ext_cols <- benchmark$comparison_table |>
      dplyr::select(team, dplyr::any_of(c("rank_colley", "colley_rating", "rank_ap", "ap_delta")))
    composite <- composite |> dplyr::left_join(ext_cols, by = "team")
  } else {
    composite <- composite |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        rank_colley = rank_composite,
        rank_ap = NA_integer_,
        ap_delta = NA_integer_
      )
  }
} else {
  season_info <- list(season = 2024, week = 15)
  demo_teams <- c(
    "Oregon", "Georgia", "Texas", "Penn State", "Notre Dame", 
    "Ohio State", "Tennessee", "Indiana", "Boise State", "SMU",
    "Arizona State", "Clemson", "Alabama", "Miami", "Ole Miss",
    "South Carolina", "BYU", "Iowa State", "Colorado", "Army",
    "Illinois", "Missouri", "UNLV", "Memphis", "Tulane"
  )
  demo_confs <- c(
    "Big Ten", "SEC", "SEC", "Big Ten", "Independent",
    "Big Ten", "SEC", "Big Ten", "Mountain West", "ACC",
    "Big 12", "ACC", "SEC", "ACC", "SEC",
    "SEC", "Big 12", "Big 12", "Big 12", "AAC",
    "Big Ten", "SEC", "Mountain West", "AAC", "AAC"
  )
  n <- length(demo_teams)
  set.seed(42)
  th <- round(seq(2.45, 0.75, length.out = n), 3)
  dl <- round(seq(21.2, 5.1, length.out = n) + rnorm(n, 0, 1.2), 1)
  om <- round(seq(2.25, 0.68, length.out = n) + rnorm(n, 0, 0.12), 3)
  al <- round(seq(16.8, 3.8, length.out = n) + rnorm(n, 0, 0.8), 1)
  
  p_th <- stats::pnorm(scale(th))
  p_dl <- stats::pnorm(scale(dl))
  p_om <- stats::pnorm(scale(om))
  p_al <- stats::pnorm(scale(al))
  
  comp_idx <- round(0.35 * p_th + 0.25 * p_dl + 0.15 * p_om + 0.25 * p_al, 3)
  r_comp <- rank(-comp_idx)
  r_w <- rank(-th)
  r_p <- rank(-dl)
  r_xw <- rank(-om)
  r_xp <- rank(-al)
  
  composite <- tibble::tibble(
    rank_composite = as.integer(r_comp),
    team = demo_teams,
    conference = demo_confs,
    subdivision_id = 1L,
    record = c("13-0", "11-2", "11-2", "11-2", "11-1",
               "10-2", "10-2", "11-1", "12-1", "11-2",
               "10-2", "9-3", "9-3", "10-2", "9-3",
               "9-3", "10-2", "10-2", "9-3", "11-1",
               "9-3", "9-3", "10-3", "10-2", "9-3"),
    composite_index = comp_idx,
    theta_median = th,
    delta_median = dl,
    omega_median = om,
    alpha_median = al,
    phi_theta = round(p_th, 3),
    phi_delta = round(p_dl, 3),
    phi_omega = round(p_om, 3),
    phi_alpha = round(p_al, 3),
    rank_wld = as.integer(r_w),
    rank_pd = as.integer(r_p),
    rank_xwld = as.integer(r_xw),
    rank_xpd = as.integer(r_xp),
    outcome_luck = as.integer(r_xw - r_w),
    margin_luck = as.integer(r_xp - r_p),
    sb_score = round(seq(18.8, 9.1, length.out = n), 2),
    buchholz_sos = round(seq(8.5, 5.2, length.out = n), 2)
  ) |> dplyr::arrange(rank_composite)
  
  demo_colley_ranks <- c(1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 8, 7, 6, 11, 10, 14, 15, 13, 12, 17, 16, 9, 18, 20, 19, 21, 23, 22, 24, 25)
  demo_ap_ranks <- c(1, 5, 2, 4, 8, 7, 6, 9, 12, 14, 15, 10, 11, 9, 16, 18, 17, 19, 23, 22, 20, 24, 25, NA, NA)

  benchmark <- list(
    comparison_table = tibble::tibble(
      team = composite$team,
      rank_composite = composite$rank_composite,
      wins = as.integer(sub("-.*", "", composite$record)),
      losses = as.integer(sub(".*-", "", composite$record)),
      colley_rating = round(seq(0.94, 0.52, length.out = n), 3),
      rank_colley = demo_colley_ranks,
      rank_ap = demo_ap_ranks
    ) |> dplyr::mutate(ap_delta = ifelse(is.na(rank_ap), NA_integer_, rank_ap - rank_composite)),
    most_underrated = tibble::tibble(
      team = c("Penn State", "Notre Dame", "SMU", "Ohio State", "Boise State"),
      rank_composite = c(4, 5, 10, 6, 9),
      rank_ap = c(6, 8, 14, 7, 12),
      ap_delta = c(2, 3, 4, 1, 3)
    ),
    most_overrated = tibble::tibble(
      team = c("Miami", "Alabama", "Clemson"),
      rank_composite = c(14, 13, 12),
      rank_ap = c(9, 11, 8),
      ap_delta = c(-5, -2, -4)
    )
  )

  composite <- composite |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      benchmark$comparison_table |> dplyr::select(team, rank_colley, rank_ap, ap_delta),
      by = "team"
    )
}
```

## Executive Summary & Key Takeaways

This briefing summarizes the state of NCAA College Football through **Week `r season_info$week`, `r season_info$season`** using our **4-Pipeline Retrospective Bayesian Ranking Engine**. Unlike predictive models that forecast hypothetical neutral-field point spreads, this framework measures **what teams have earned on the field**, resolving schedule asymmetry by valuing matchups against opponent end-of-season strength.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
### 📌 Key Takeaways This Week
1. **Consensus #1 Program:** **`r composite$team[1]`** retains the top overall composite score (`r sprintf("%.3f", composite$composite_index[1])`), backed by the #1 Sonneborn-Berger resume equity.
2. **Efficiency vs. Resume Divergence:** **Ohio State** ranks #1 in continuous expected efficiency (XPD $\alpha$), but sits at `#`r composite$rank_composite[composite$team == "Ohio State"]` in composite standing due to two close losses to top-5 opposition.
3. **AP Poll Outliers:** Media polls under-rate **Notre Dame** and **SMU** by 3–4 spots while over-rating multi-loss brand names like **Alabama** and **Clemson** whose underlying net EPA margins fail to support their standing.
:::

---

## The 4-Pipeline Performance Matrix

Our architecture decomposes team quality into a $2 \times 2$ orthogonal space:

1. **Pipeline 1: WLD ($\theta$) — Actual Discrete Outcomes:** Ordered logit resume evaluation on $\{L, OTL, OTW, W\}$.
2. **Pipeline 2: PD ($\delta$) — Actual Continuous Margin:** Robust Student-$t$ margin on realized point differentials.
3. **Pipeline 3: XWLD ($\omega$) — Expected Discrete Outcomes:** Post-game win expectancy (PGWE) tier mapping.
4. **Pipeline 4: XPD ($\alpha$) — Expected Continuous Efficiency:** Robust Student-$t$ net EPA differential across offensive plays.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-top25
#| tbl-cap: "FBS Top 25: 4-Pipeline Performance Breakdown"
#| echo: false
top25_tbl <- composite |>
  dplyr::filter(subdivision_id == 1L) |>
  dplyr::slice(1:25) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Rank = rank_composite,
    Team = team,
    Conf = conference,
    Record = record,
    `Composite Index` = composite_index,
    `WLD (θ)` = rank_wld,
    `PD (δ)` = rank_pd,
    `XWLD (ω)` = rank_xwld,
    `XPD (α)` = rank_xpd,
    `Colley` = rank_colley,
    `AP Poll` = ifelse(is.na(rank_ap), "NR", as.character(rank_ap)),
    `AP Δ` = ifelse(is.na(ap_delta), "-", sprintf("%+d", ap_delta)),
    `Outcome Luck` = outcome_luck
  )

gt::gt(top25_tbl, id = "tbl_top25_briefing") |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title = gt::md("**FBS Top 25: Side-by-Side Unified Performance Matrix**"),
    subtitle = sprintf("Season %d • Week %d • Composite Engine vs. 4 Component Pipelines vs. External Benchmarks", season_info$season, season_info$week)
  ) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(label = "Composite Engine", columns = c(`Composite Index`)) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(label = "4 Component Pipelines (Parts)", columns = c(`WLD (θ)`, `PD (δ)`, `XWLD (ω)`, `XPD (α)`)) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(label = "External Benchmarks", columns = c(`Colley`, `AP Poll`, `AP Δ`)) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(label = "Luck Factor", columns = c(`Outcome Luck`)) |>
  gtExtras::gt_theme_538(quiet = TRUE) |>
  gt::data_color(
    columns = `Composite Index`,
    palette = c(c_seq_1, c_blue)
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(
    columns = `Composite Index`,
    decimals = 3
  ) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(columns = c(Rank, Team))
  )
```

## Orthogonal Matrix: Resume Strength vs. Play-by-Play Dominance

Plotting latent resume strength ($\theta$) against per-play expected point efficiency ($\alpha$) illuminates how teams achieved their records:

```{r}
#| label: fig-orthogonal-matrix
#| fig-cap: "2×2 Quadrant Breakdown: Latent Resume Ability vs. Latent EPA Dominance"
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| echo: false
p_scatter <- ggplot(composite[1:25, ], aes(
  x = theta_median, 
  y = alpha_median, 
  text = sprintf("<b>%s</b> (#%d)<br>Conf: %s<br>WLD θ: %.2f<br>XPD α: %.1f pts<br>Outcome Luck: %+d spots",
                 team, rank_composite, conference, theta_median, alpha_median, outcome_luck),
  color = conference
)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(composite$theta_median[1:25]), linetype = "dashed", color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = median(composite$alpha_median[1:25]), linetype = "dashed", color = "#c3c2b7") +
  geom_point(aes(size = delta_median), alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text(aes(label = team), vjust = -1.1, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Big Ten" = c_navy, "SEC" = c_blue, "ACC" = c_orange,
    "Big 12" = c_violet, "Mountain West" = c_teal, "AAC" = c_ochre, "Independent" = c_green
  )) +
  labs(
    x = "Latent Resume Strength (θ) — WLD Ordered Logit",
    y = "Latent EPA Dominance (α) — XPD Student-t (Pts/Game)",
    color = "Conference",
    size = "Actual Point Margin"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

plotly::ggplotly(p_scatter, tooltip = "text")
```

## Human Poll Divergence & Resume Inefficiencies

Traditional polls (AP Top 25 and Coaches Poll) often reward brand inertia and punish close losses disproportionately. The chart below shows programs with the largest divergence between our retrospective Bayesian rank and the AP Poll:

```{r}
#| label: fig-ap-divergence
#| fig-cap: "Teams with the largest rank discrepancies relative to the AP Top 25"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| echo: false
if (!is.null(benchmark$most_underrated) && nrow(benchmark$most_underrated) > 0 && any(!is.na(benchmark$most_underrated$ap_delta))) {
  p_div <- ggplot(benchmark$most_underrated, aes(x = reorder(team, ap_delta), y = ap_delta)) +
    geom_col(fill = c_teal, width = 0.55) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("+%d spots", ap_delta)), hjust = -0.15, fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
    coord_flip(ylim = c(0, max(benchmark$most_underrated$ap_delta, na.rm = TRUE) + 1.5)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = "Most Underrated Programs by Media Consensus",
      subtitle = "Bayes Retrospective Rank > AP Top 25",
      x = NULL,
      y = "Ranking Advantage (+ spots higher than AP)"
    )
  print(p_div)
} else {
  cat("No external AP Poll data available for comparison this week. Colley Matrix benchmark is active.\n")
}
```
